name: sap-ui-automation
description: See and drive the SAP screens you have open: SAP GUI for Windows, Web GUI and Fiori, as a compact text view.
long_description:
Lets Claude see and drive the SAP screens you already have open, under your own SAP authorisations: **SAP GUI for Windows** (through SAP GUI scripting), **SAP GUI for HTML (Web GUI)** and **SAP Fiori** in Chrome.

It finds your open sessions by itself, reads each screen as one line per control with SAP's own ids, and acts on those ids. It never logs on and never stores a password.

**Writes are refused by default** (`SAP_WRITE` = off). Set it to `confirm` to approve each action that may write to SAP, or `on` to allow them. You can also limit the systems, transactions and browser origins it may touch.

Web GUI and Fiori need Chrome (or Edge) with remote debugging allowed: open chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging once. See the documentation for details.

tools.name: sap_sessions
tools.description: Lists the SAP sessions open on this machine (SAP GUI windows, Web GUI and Fiori tabs in Chrome).

tools.name: sap_use
tools.description: Makes another session the active one.

tools.name: sap_look
tools.description: The current SAP screen as compact text: one line per control with its id, label, value and state.

tools.name: sap_act
tools.description: One action on the active SAP screen, by an id from sap_look; answers with the new screen or what changed.

tools.name: sap_screenshot
tools.description: A PNG of the session's window or tab.

tools.name: sap_record
tools.description: Records the run as a test: start, stop, checks, variables, export.

tools.name: sap_replay
tools.description: Runs a recorded test again, with no model.

SAP_WRITE.title: Writes to SAP (SAP_WRITE)
SAP_WRITE.description: off: actions that may write to SAP are refused (default). confirm: you are asked before each one, if Claude Desktop supports it (MCP elicitation, not documented); otherwise they are refused. on: they run.

SAP_ALLOW_SYSTEMS.title: Allowed systems (SAP_ALLOW_SYSTEMS)
SAP_ALLOW_SYSTEMS.description: Only these systems, optionally with client, comma separated, for example ABA/800, S4H. Empty: every system.

SAP_ALLOW_TCODES.title: Allowed transactions (SAP_ALLOW_TCODES)
SAP_ALLOW_TCODES.description: Only these transactions may be opened or worked in, comma separated, for example VA03, MM03. Empty: no allow list.

SAP_BLOCK_TCODES.title: Blocked transactions (SAP_BLOCK_TCODES)
SAP_BLOCK_TCODES.description: Transactions the agent may not open or work in, comma separated, for example SE38, SU01.

SAP_ALLOW_ORIGINS.title: Allowed browser origins (SAP_ALLOW_ORIGINS)
SAP_ALLOW_ORIGINS.description: Web GUI and Fiori: only browser tabs of these origins, comma separated, for example https://myhost:44300. Empty: any SAP tab.

SAP_SURFACES.title: Surfaces (SAP_SURFACES)
SAP_SURFACES.description: Which kinds of session to look for, comma separated: sapgui, webgui, fiori. Empty: all that apply on this machine.

SAP_CHROME_CDP.title: Chrome DevTools endpoint (SAP_CHROME_CDP)
SAP_CHROME_CDP.description: A Chrome DevTools endpoint to attach to, for example http://127.0.0.1:9222. Empty: the running Chrome or Edge that allows remote debugging.

SAP_RECORD_DIR.title: Recordings folder (SAP_RECORD_DIR)
SAP_RECORD_DIR.description: Where sap_record writes recordings and exports. Pick a folder you can write to, for example one in Documents. Empty: sap-tests in the folder Claude starts the server in.
